utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I thought I should make myself available in case there are any outstanding issues in relation to tomorrow's timetable of Mr. Donia giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, thank you for coming. I discussed it with my colleagues and the Chamber would prefer first to deal with Mr. Mehonic, who is waiting, then see whether there are any remaining issues in relation to Mr. Donia's report, and then continue with Witness Q. Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please guide Mr. Mehonic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I be excused, Mr. President, until that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I expect that Mr. Mehonic will take only not many minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will wait, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehonic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehonic, the Prosecution has asked leave to recall you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, it was only a matter to retrieve from him his original certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Mehonic, were you able to locate your original medical certificate or that copy that you got from the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RASIM MEHONIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And would you be prepared to release it to us if you obtained a certified copy from us?

utterances.speaker: RASIM MEHONIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't get the original then, if you take the original. Because that's a permanent document for me, one that will last for a lifetime

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, perhaps we had best ask for another copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mehonic, I think there are two ways of doing it: If you would give us the original, you would receive from the Tribunal a copy that is certified. That means that it is indicated on the copy that this is the same as the original; otherwise, if you would give us the -- if you would give us your original, just for inspection to start with, and that we could then perhaps prepare a copy. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A third option, if I may actually propose it, is to have him compare his original with the one tendered in evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps have the original inspected by the Defence as well and by the Chamber as well. Yes. Mr. Mehonic, would you agree to give your original for inspection to all the parties --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we will return it to you and you could compare your original with the copy already made, and perhaps questions are put to you in this respect. So if you would give your original to the usher, and I promise you, you will get it back. If you would please first give it to the Defence. Will you then please give it to Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall comment on this perhaps later when we conduct the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, may I give the original to you so that you can take care of a copy to be prepared for the witness and then return the original -- no, the copy, to be prepared for us. Yes. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have nothing further to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you have any questions in particular to the document just shown, you may please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. To tell you the truth, we don't have any particular questions apart for one. Could we ask the witness whether he could explain to this Trial Chamber why this document was manipulated, that is what we have called it? And this seems to be the case because in the original there is something marked in blue at the bottom of the document, and grey or black was used for what has been inscribed on the upper part of the document. I am not talking about the form, Mr. President. I am talking about the text that was superimposed, that was added to the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you tell us why this document is presented in two colours, has two colours?

utterances.speaker: RASIM MEHONIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question. The person who made the document could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Which document is going to be tendered, all of them or the -- Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would propose that the document originally tendered by the Prosecution received in evidence, we would do the minor amendment to the translation in due course. The Court has asked to see the original and the Court has had an opportunity to compare them. I am not aware that there is any substantial difference between the original and the one that the Prosecution tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then you intend to tender a different translation. That means P1517C.1 will be replaced by another translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, and that translation would only delete the date of discharge or the date inserted in the column for the date of discharge. That would be the only change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear to me. Mr. Mehonic, may I ask the parties whether it is necessary to make any additional copy or that P1517, which seems to be a copy of the document we just saw. I don't think that there is any need to make an additional copy, but if one of the parties would not agree, I would like to hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but I would like it to be clear and that the Prosecution also admits that the original, which was filed, apparently has two different types of writing because we can see this in the original but not in the copy. So if the Prosecution admits that it seems to me there were two types of printing on this document, that is fine. But if that is not the case, then we need a colour copy, I think, in order to be able to locate this problem subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am afraid I am not in a position to make that concession, Mr. President. Perhaps I could have a look at the original again to see if I could identify what my friend is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring to is that part of the entries are in black, while the box on "diagnoza" and "epicrisis" are in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution is prepared to concede that a number which is apparently written by hand, written with a blue pen, is in blue, whereas on the photocopy, it is in black. The signature on the doctor appears to be in blue, where, on the photocopy, it is in black. And There are other printed writing on the original document which is in blue print whereas they are identically copied on the photocopy, except on the photocopy, they are in black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But whatever the importance of that might be, whatever -- perhaps it is good to have a colour copy, since the Defence raised the issue, and then for the future, we always be sure on what is in blue and what is in black. So if the Chamber would prefer to have a coloured copy tendered, then so it should be made then this afternoon. I think it would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. So we will have a colour copy prepared. May I just ensure that that is possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registry could do it, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps we could ask the Registry to do it. We could, but we could not guarantee it to be returned today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please return it to the Registrar. Mr. Mehonic, the Registry will, in approximately one hour, one hour and a half, prepare a colour copy of the document and then the original will be returned to you again. If that is all right with you? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, may I then draw your attention that the ERN number seems to be added on the copy that it's entered this time, that whenever the colour copy is ready, that we give it to you so that you can fill in whatever ERN number should be on the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehonic, you have been in the courtroom only for a very short period this afternoon and you know that we would like to see the original of your discharge letter. But let me return to your testimony. You have answered all the questions of the parties. You have also answered our questions. We also have noticed that it was painful for you to be taken back to the moments which I assume would be among the most painful in your life. We are aware of that. We noticed it. You will understand that we are grateful that you have taken the effort to come to The Hague to answer the questions of the parties and the question of the Judges, because I hope that you are aware that it is important for this Chamber to hear the answers to these questions from those who have been present at that time and at these places. So we thank you very much for that, and we hope you have a safe journey home again. I think the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Witness and Victims Unit will help you recover the original. That will be done during the next break that will be in approximately in one hour. Thank you very much for coming again. Mr. Usher, will you please escort Mr. Mehonic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, we will decide on 1517C once we have received the -- and when the Prosecution has tendered the coloured copy of it. Is there anything else? No, there is nothing else. It was the only document used. That means that we could now briefly pay attention to whether there are any remaining issues in respect of the documents attached to the report of Mr. Donia or whatever pages. Yes, one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, meanwhile, the technicians might work on the preparation of the protective measures for Witness Q. Whom of the parties may I invite to speak first on the issue of the documents in relation to Mr. Donia's report?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to update the Trial Chamber, Mr. President. As I understand it, in various requests made by the Defence for disclosure of further material, firstly in respect of the copies of Oslobodjenje and other publications, there is one issue of that newspaper and an issue of another publication still to come. We have also located a copy of -- tape-recording, rather, of the speech by Radovan Karadzic which the Defence has requested. We are making a copy of that. We will disclose both a tape-recording and a transcription into B/C/S and a translation into English. I anticipate that the Defence will receive that material this afternoon. As far as I am aware, Mr. President, they are the outstanding issues in relation to the documents

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just check with the Defence whether they agree that these were the outstanding issues. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially, Mr. President. Partially. Partially, because although we have received certain documents mentioned by the Prosecution, it appears that as far as the last ones are concerned, we received them at a very late date, that is to say either this morning -- or I can see here a date. It says the 17th of April, so that was today. And we think that it is not possible to submit such a quantity of documents in one language a few days or a few hours before such an important hearing as to the case with this witness. As far as the cassette is concerned, first of all, it was said that such a cassette does not exist. It is now a pleasure to see that it does exist and it shall soon be produced, but if I have understood everything correctly. But we are lacking time. We don't have enough time to prepare our Defence. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, two matters: Firstly, I did not say yesterday or on any other occasion that the tape did not exist. I said I would check to see whether we had a copy and made it clear that the footnote did not refer to a tape but, rather, a transcription. Secondly, my friend complains that the material is being provided to him late. The newspaper items were requested by the Defence by letter dated the 13th of April and they were provided, in the main part, yesterday and the day before. The Defence has had the report since the 25th of February so they have sought this material very late. Secondly, or further in relation to that point, we have made clear that this material is open source. It was available to them to obtain in any event, but rather than make an issue of it, we have simply provided it to them. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I suggest that we proceed as far as we can come, and if there is any specific moment where you say we can't proceed for specifically this or that reason or that there is some information in the material which has been provided to you recently - I am not expressing any view of the Chamber on whether this was an obligatory providing of this material or whether it was courtesy - but if we come at a point where you say for this and this reasons, we are handicapped [Real-time transcript read in error "you are handicapped"] specifically, please let the Chamber know so that we can see what to do under these circumstances. But we have taken notice that you feel in a general way handicapped by receiving late these copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for this suggestion. The Defence shall take note of it, if necessary. But as far as the material is concerned the material that has been presented as open source material, this is mostly -- these are mostly newspapers which were published in Sarajevo and which weren't distributed internationally, and it is obviously very difficult for the Defence to find newspaper articles which come from certain issues since all of this took place in Sarajevo and these newspapers weren't distributed elsewhere. So I don't think it is quite correct to say that this material was publicly available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd say in general terms it was, but you said it was not easily accessible to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the transcript, I think in page 10, line one, it says: "We are handicapped," and I think that you said, "You are handicapped."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say that you are handicapped. Whether the Chamber is handicapped is for ourselves to decide and to solve. Mr. Stamp is the Prosecution then ready to resume the examination of Witness Q? And may I ask the technical booth that every measure, that means facial distortion, voice distortion, is effective at this very moment. So it is confirmed by the technical booth that everything is effective. It is now up to us to use our microphones in such a way that it remains effective and also up to us to not mention any name or any other identifying details. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in Witness Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I be excused, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Q, as I still call you, can you hear me in a language you understand? Thank you. Please be seated. It is perhaps unnecessary but I nevertheless remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness Q, yesterday we were looking at the photographs which you said you took, and we had looked at photograph 1 and photograph 2, which were taken -- these photographs were taken of the impact sites in front of number 3 Cetinska Street. Could he be given back that Exhibit P2172?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist. Do you have the page already in mind, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Page 1 and page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please put page 1 on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You had indicated that the arrows in photograph on page 1 and photograph on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, but we still sometimes have this problem with the translation. P21312 312 was what I heard in the French translation and here it says P222 -- I mean, we will need this to be reflected correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document, for the record, is P2172, which has been handed to the witness. And that has been confirmed by the Registrar: P2172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the impact site in photograph 1 and photograph 2 are on a road?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't hear the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters have some difficulties in hearing you. It would be the centre microphone. Perhaps if you come a bit closer to the microphone in the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Perhaps switching on the microphone wouldn't be a bad idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I hear that switching on the microphone would be a good idea as well. Yes, it doesn't help if you come closer if it's switched off. Would you please speak a few words to see whether the interpreters can hear you correctly now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not a word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is still a problem. Perhaps we switched it off by now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is okay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Those arrows in photograph 1 and photograph 2 point to an impact site in the middle of the road, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that they represent the site of the explosion. As to whether it is exactly in the middle of the road, I am not certain. But it is certainly on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is there a building at 3 Cetinska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way this photo is taken, the Cetinska building number 3 is supposedly behind the back of the photographer, that is to say I, myself, when I was taking this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you referring to photograph 1 when you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture I see on the screen, I believe that is picture number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please look on the ELMO and confirm that you are speaking of picture number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's picture number 1. Behind my back more or less would be the residential building number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, that is what I wanted to enquire into. This residential building was about how far from the impact site that you photographed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps from the site of the explosion to the building itself -- well, it was probably an approximate distance of 20 metres. I can't tell, but about 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at photograph on page number 3 of the booklet. Could you just read what you wrote on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that photo number 3 represents the traces of the explosion of the shell on the asphalt in Cetinska Street next to the building number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And on that photograph there is a yellow line or a yellow instrument across the middle of the photograph. Could you say what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the photo can be a part of the tape that we use to place on the traces of the explosion so that we were able to take measurements afterwards, basically, in order to make it visible on the photograph what the size of the area was because we all knew the dimensions of that tape. I mean, we didn't actually use it to measure anything; we just put it on the photo in order to make it clear what the dimensions were. Today we've got better equipment and, at the time, we didn't have anything else so we made do with what we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you have a look at photo number 4. Could you read what you wrote under that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photo 4: "Traces of blood in the vicinity of the spot where the shell exploded."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you recall which impact site this was? Was it the one at Cetinska street or Klara Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain, but if I look at the sequence of these pictures, it is probably by the first explosion site.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at photo number 5, please. Could you read what you have written below that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photo 5: "The place in Klara Zetkin Street next to the house number 4 where the shell landed."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is this house number 4 another residential apartment block?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "residential area."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I didn't say area, I said block. May I repeat it? Well, let us have a look at the photograph. You have an arrow on the photograph. What does that arrow point to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow indicates the place of the explosion. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the background of that photograph, do you see some stairs and then entrance to a building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's the building behind the site of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is that -- what type of building is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: A multi-storey building. There was a whole row of multi-storey buildings. That means that they were residential buildings, several floors and several entrances. It is possible that two entrances may be seen on this picture, but it is a bit dark here on the screen so I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you wish to, you may have a look at the copy on the ELMO. If it could remain there, though. Could you have a look at photo number 6, please. Is that a close-up photograph of the impact site in front of Klara Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the tracer that was seen on picture number 5 which was marked by an arrow on picture number 5. So it is the same photo but from a lesser distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the impact site was, from these photographs -- would you agree with me that the site was on the sidewalk in front of the building, on the edge of the sidewalk in front of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the damage, we can see that it was on the edge of the pavement and part of the road, so that's just the edge of the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you have a look at photo number 6. Photo number 7, I beg your pardon. Could you read what you have written below that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photo 7: "Traces of blood and tissue and children's sleigh."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you now have a look at photo number 8 and tell us what you have written below that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photo number 8: "Child's cap in the snow and traces of blood in the background."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher, you may remove that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to this incident and the work that you did there, did you file a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And would you be able to identify that report from or a copy of that report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, may he be shown document P2171B?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, unfortunately, there is interference and we can't hear the speaker again. I think somebody's mobile phone is interfering with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear everyone although very -- at a low level. Is it the witness you can't hear or is it someone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] I can hear everyone but the booth can't hear me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please test.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, now it is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please then proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason why I decided to stand up was that the interpreters did not mention the number of the document. So for the transcript, I think it would be a good idea to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed I will. P2171B.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at that document, please. Do you see on that document a copy of your signature or your signature photocopied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that the report you filed on the 22nd -- I beg your pardon. Is that the report you filed in respect to the incident of the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness, with your leave, be shown a document which is recalled, it is already in evidence, document P2171? P2171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is without the B?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Without the B.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a ballistic report signed by Borislav Stankov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you look in the second paragraph of that document, do you see [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must intervene once again because I am afraid that these questions might damage the protection of the witness, and also for the transcript, the term "forensic expert," should perhaps be checked out in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the expression I used -- well, the expression in the English transcript is "forensic officer." I am quite sure that the French expression in respect to "forensic expert," can be checked and will be corrected with them or their tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But may I just say to the witness, Witness, I am not asking you to say or to read what you see or to say your name. Do you see [redacted] [redacted]; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this report is a ballistic report for the shelling incident that you have just testified about, that is incident on the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I propose to show to the witness document 2171A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you remain to help him, Mr. Usher, if need be. Could you remain to help him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the purpose of the transcript, the number in 19-3 is not the number is marked on the document. One digit is missing, a "1," I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, for the record, the number which has been handed to the witness -- the number of the document which has been handed to the witness is 2171A, number 2171A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you compare those two documents, that is document 2171A and document 2171?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can see, they appear to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should clarify things in the transcript for the future because there is a great deal of confusion. It is 217 and we need to make everything clear because there is a confusion here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the speaker please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And I think that somebody referred to a "C" document, one of the booths, but I don't know what it refers to. If the Prosecution could just refer to both of these documents clearly so that there is no confusion in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And please help him, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Have a look at document P2171. Document P2171. On the second page of that document, do you see that some of the lines in the first paragraph are blurred and illegible or almost illegible? Please answer, "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are illegible; it is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now look at document P2171A. [Real-time transcript read in error "P217"]. Would you agree with me that the -- that document which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask for the transcript again, the last number, Mr. Stamp mentioned was P2171A. It appeared a different number in the transcript. Are there any technical problems in reproducing these numbers in the transcript because then I would like to know. Because when I repeat the number, it does not appear in the transcript either. So I mentioned P2171A. I'll try to repeat it: P2171A. May I ask specifically to those who are reviewing the transcript overnight and may I invite the parties to check whether, after having listened to the audio tape, whether the numbers appear in a good order in the transcript and let me do it this way. The first document Mr. Stamp asked the witness to have a look at was a previously already admitted document of which the translation is partly in black because of the bad legibility of that document. The second document Mr. Stamp mentioned is a document of which the witness said that it appeared to be the same document, and I think the parties would agree that this is a party [sic] which appears to be the same, but legible in its entirety. If the parties could agree on that, then we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just want to verify something. I think we could agree on this point, as I think that we could agree that this clear document could have been submitted to us at a much earlier date, and to the Trial Chamber too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you will just leave me one moment. Yes, if it is any different, I will hear from you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I also said that it "appeared" to be. I didn't say that it is the same document, but it appears to be the same document. I wonder whether, if numbers are mentioned, whether the court reporters could do it by words, rather than by numbers. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could you, Mr. Usher, take away document P2171 and leave the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I specifically thank the court reporters for helping us out of the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, could you now return to document P2171B, which is the report you signed. In that document you refer to the place and time of the act that you investigated, and could you read what the reference is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Klara Zetkin Street and Cetinska number 3, 23rd of January, 1994, at about 1315 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At section number four of your document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, if I may interrupt you. I heard "23rd of January" and that is also what appears in the transcript. Could you please clarify this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you are recorded for the place and time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Klara Zetkin Street number 4, Cetinska number 3, the 22nd of January, 1994, at about 1315 hours."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And at item number 4, the description of the criminal act, could you please read what you have recorded there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 22nd of January, 1994, at about 1315 hours, [from the west Nedzarici] two mortar shells fell, the calibre of which was 120 millimetres. They fell at Klara Zetkin street number 4 and the other fell at Cetinska Street number 3. On that occasion, several people were killed and -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you pause there, please. We will get to the casualties shortly. You just had a look at the document, the forensic -- the ballistic report signed by Borislav Stankov. In that report, it indicates that the impact sites on Klara Zetkin Street and Cetinska Street, from their examination, were caused by 82 millimetre mortars. Is that correct from what you see on the report of Borislav Stankov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Borislav Stankov is a forensic expert. I was dealing with another issue. He is an expert, too, and on the basis of traces, he decides, he comes to a conclusion as to what projectile was used. So that his findings shall be recorded and shall be taken to be valid before mine is, which was written immediately after the event itself. Without having made any investigations, without having questioned anyone, but on the basis of what I myself saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Borislav Stankov is a ballistic expert; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this question is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... about whether Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In general, Mr. President, we sometimes contest the authenticity of the -- the quality of the experts for some persons, in the case of some persons who signed certain documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a different matter compared to whether it is in dispute that he is known as perhaps an expert in a certain field. But if you insist, then I will ask Mr. Stamp to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the document signed by Borislav Stankov, could you read the first paragraph or the heading of the document? That is P2171A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Record of forensic investigation carried out at the site where shells fell in Cetinska Street and Klara Zetkin Street and also in the park between Klara Zetkin Street and the Rade Koncera Square, written by Borislav Stankov, a ballistics expert with the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a ballistic expert at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you wrote -- or may I just ask him a leading question. On what basis did you write two-120 millimetre mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote this under the description of the act itself, that's under paragraph four, number four. And here on the second page under number six paragraph -- the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Why did you write 120 millimetre mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the site where these two shells exploded, I investigated the site, I determined what had happened. I took some photographs. First of all, there is a little inspection and then the photographs were taken. And at that site I found here, it says, "the tail of the shell." The situation was such that I had to investigate the entire site myself. So in usual case the custom was for several of us to go and investigate such sites, but in this case, I was on my own. And I found that shell tail, the tail of a 120 millimetre shell, and it is on the basis of that that I wrote this report after I had carried out the on-site investigation. And the measurements and other things, they were carried out by the ballistic experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the French transcript, it says "localization" instead of "location." I think there was a mistake there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What the Judges sometimes do, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is to write down the page number and line number and then the word as you see it in the transcript and the word you had spoken, because this might not create whatever confusion, and we would be grateful if you would assist those who are preparing the transcript and, at the same time, not interrupt unnecessarily the examination-in-chief. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You had reached to reading about the casualties on the item four of your report. Could you read for us that part of your report.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On that occasion, several people were wounded and Subasic Admir died, [born in 1986]; Nermin Rizvanovic, [date of birth 1981]; Jasmina Brkovic [date of birth, 1989]; Indira Brkovic," in brackets, I can't see the exact year; "Mirza Dedovic [1986]; Daniel Jurinic, [1983]."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And were these the fatalities from the incident that you discovered as a result of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the names of the people who died and the names that I obtained after I had carried out the on-site investigation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you lived in Alipasino Polje at the time and the community of Alipasino Polje was also a part of your police district. Can you tell us please, generally speaking, about the shelling that occurred in your district.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean for the entire period of time or just for this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay, I'm a little bit vague there. You said the area was not shelled for about 26 days before this incident. Do you know why the area was not shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question. I don't know why it wasn't shelled. I was very glad that there was no shelling. I was glad that that was not repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, prior to the beginning of this 26 days before the incident, was the area -- to what degree was the area shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly how much shelling there was because -- I can't exactly remember how much shelling there was. But there was also four because there was also very nearby. Vojnicko Polje, Alipasino Polje, which was divided into areas where exactly the shells fell, and they fell in a discriminate manner in these areas. I couldn't say exactly. I can't say whether they fell in those areas and I couldn't say how many shells fell. But in the entire area of Alipasino Polje, I am sure that 26 days prior to this incident there was no shelling. So there was a period of peace right up until this shelling. And as to what happened after that shelling, I can't remember because shells continued to fall after this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any local arrangements between the two armies at around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was just doing my job and I was happy to say that there was a peaceful period. Whether some agreement had been reached about the peace, I don't know. I can't remember whether there was electricity at the time to enable people to follow the news and the media. Whether there was some sort of agreement, I really couldn't answer that question precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you -- as a resident of Alipasino Polje, you told us that the shelling was sometime indiscriminate in the area. Could you from your experience determine sometimes where the shells were fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sarajevo was a town that was surrounded. Our greatest fear in that area was -- our greatest fears concerned the Nedzarici area, the Nedzarici settlement, the Lukavica settlement. That is an area which is behind the Mojmilo hill, the Mojmilo Brdo, and part of the airport settlement which is right next to the Nedzarici area. As I wasn't always working in Alipasino Polje but also in the town during the war period, Dobrinja was also an area in which I worked and which I carried out certain on-site investigations, and it was very difficult to move from the Alipasino Polje area to Dobrinja because that part was an open area and it was easily visible from the Nedzarici area. On certain occasions I had to wait for night to fall. Sometimes I would even sleep over in Dobrinja. So Nedzarici was directly visible from my sight and Lukavica area was not visible, but it was possible to shell from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just take you back to what I was asking you about. From your experience of living in Alipasino Polje, could you sometimes determine from where shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was able to determine that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How could one do that? How were you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unable to determine the direction from which the shell came, but it was very difficult to determine the actual place from which the shell was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How would you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible to do so on the basis of the traces that would be left after the explosion of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You, in your report, if you have a look at it, please, and that is P2171B, on item 4 you indicated that the shells came from Nedzarici. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On what basis did you write that? Why did you write that? Did you receive any information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: To determine the direction from which a shell came, I was able to determine that myself on the basis of the traces that I would discover at the site. On that basis, it was possible to determine that the shell had come from the west, and Nedzarici is in that direction. Nedzarici is to the west and that is why I wrote down Nedzarici in brackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you were not at home in Alipasino Polje at the time of this incident, but you were at your office and you were called there. Had you ever been at home when the -- when anywhere near you was shelled from Nedzarici? I beg your pardon, had you ever been at home in Alipasino Polje where any position near where you were was shelled from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I experienced quite a bit of shelling but I can't remember exactly whether some of the shelling came from the Nedzarici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you can't recall exactly whether some of the shelling came from the Nedzarici area. Can you recall anything about any other shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean some cases for which I carried out the on-site investigations or cases in which I was either in my flat or perhaps in the streets, in squares, and there was shelling in the surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I am asking about your experience living in Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in Alipasino Polje and I experienced quite a lot of shelling, but while I was in my flat because that was the safest place to be if I was not working. And in my opinion, it would be pointless to go to the site of the explosion itself since, from my personal experience, and this was possible to see on the basis of the on-site investigations, it was very dangerous to go to see where the shell had come from, from which direction, because it was possible for other shells to be fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your flat or the area where you lived in Alipasino Polje, did you hear shells being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was possible to hear them and I did hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you can, some of the places where you have heard shells being fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici was the closest place from which you could hear shells being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, apart from the investigation of the 22nd of January, 1994, you conducted, as you indicated, many other investigations. I would like to take you to one in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, before doing so, we are close to a quarter to 4.00 and it seems that you enter a new area. Would this be a suitable moment to have the break or...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And can you give us an indication how much time you'd still need for the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately ten minutes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Q and all the others in this courtroom, we will adjourn until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 4.17 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the interval I indicated I wanted to take you to another investigation, but before I do that, may I ask you just a couple further questions about your experiences living in Alipasino Polje. You said that Nedzarici was the closest place from which you could hear shells being fired. Could you say under the control of which party in the conflict was Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, apparently there is no translation. There is some technical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of Mr. Stamp or not of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just, slowly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I do hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem seems to be solved. Mr. Stamp, I think that is the moment to resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Firstly, could you tell us which party to the conflict, was it the Bosnian Serb army or the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that controlled the community of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici was controlled by the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you could hear shells being fired from Nedzarici from the vicinity of your home in Alipasino Polje. Could you describe what you mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often while I was living in Alipasino Polje and in the course of shelling, prior to the explosions in Alipasino Polje, we could hear muffled sound and we usually concluded that it was a sound of those shells being fired, the shells that later on landed onto our area. So there is a big difference between that sound and the actual explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Taking you now to the 10th -- to the 9th, I beg your pardon, of November, 1993. Did you investigate shellings in Alipasino Polje which occurred on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I carried out the on-site investigation of the 9th of November, 1993, but I don't know exactly what particular case you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us then how many cases of shelling were there on the 9th of November 1993 in Alipasino Polje that you was involved in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I carried out the on-site investigation for two shells and I can remember those two cases. As to whether there were any more shellings, I don't know. But I do remember that I carried out two on-site investigations for two cases of shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did these two cases occur? Can you remember the street names of the places where these shellings occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first on-site investigation was in Alipasino Polje "B" Faza is the name of the district, and the street is Trg Zavnobih.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the other on-site investigation was where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other on-site investigation was in an area called "C" Faza, Trg Rade Koncara -- Rade Koncara Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us from your investigations how many shells landed at Trg Zavnobih?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: One shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did it land in the vicinity of any particular building or structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shell landed on the pavement behind the building on Zavnobih Square, where there was a school. Those were the premises of a primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And from your investigations, can you say whether or not there were any casualties as a result of that shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: In as far as the Zavnobih Square investigation is concerned, when the shell exploded in the vicinity of the school, I do know that a teacher died and two -- and three children as well. As to the number of casualties, the number of survivors, I don't know exactly. I believe there could have been about 20, perhaps even more. Anyway, this was the task of other people on the team. After the on-site investigation, they had to mark in their reports as to how many casualties there were and whether they were lightly wounded or heavily wounded or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your investigations, can you say whether school was in session at the time of that shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered the building where the teaching was taking place, judging by the objects found on the premises, there must have been lessons going on because I found traces of clothes on the chairs, books; there was a blackboard, so it seemed to indicate that teaching was underway and then it was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a certain number of pictures, but from the outside, since the building itself where this make-shift classroom was situated was surrounded by cement blocks and it was dark in the classroom itself, so as to be able to make the pictures on the other side, and I did not have a flash on my camera so I could only take pictures of the traces I found outside around the site of the explosion. And for technical reasons, I was unable to take pictures on the inside. I could just describe it on the basis of what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you bring those photographs with you when you travelled to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as in the case of all the other cases, so as to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, may I tender to the witness Exhibit P3681.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Mr. Usher, could you please assist Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There may be a slight misunderstanding. I have just been told that the reproductions were just made today and it may well be that my friends are just receiving a copy of this document. I don't know if they were served with it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Everything is perfect. We did have a copy. We have had it for five seconds, perhaps seven or eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means, Mr. Stamp, that if the Defence would ask more time to prepare for cross-examination, that it would only be fair to give it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We would not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, the thing is, we have copies which are partly legible. I don't know if these are the same ones. But generally speaking, the Defence, which is only made up of two members, would like to discuss all that within the team. This is not the first time, although we don't probably have records of every single case, but we are given these documents at the eleventh hour. As a consequence, we would like to be able to consult with all the members of our team, and if the Bench authorises us to do so, we will have the witness come back at an appropriate time. Once we have had the time to prepare, not in a normal manner but perhaps in a satisfactory, partly satisfactory manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's see where we go. I make one observation. The Chamber will not accept the claim that every member of the team has always seen all documents, but that is not the same as that the Defence should get a reasonable time to study photographs that have been newly introduced. At the same time, we understand from the Prosecution that they only recently received these photographs. Am I right in my understanding, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So let us first continue the examination-in-chief and we'll see how much time you would need and the Defence would need to prepare for cross-examination on this specific issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I remember correctly, this witness was here yesterday and if he came from Sarajevo yesterday, he must have had those pictures yesterday, and no doubt the Prosecution was preparing the witness the day before yesterday and they must have seen the documents and the pictures the day before yesterday. So it's just a matter of simple courtesy. I believe the Prosecution has been familiar with this for some time now and it is not by accident that we are being given the documents only now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Q, when did you first indicate to the Prosecution that you had these photographs and when did you first show to them, to the representatives of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday. Yesterday morning, to be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You showed them for the first time or you indicated that you would have them yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both. I told them I had them and I showed them to them because they were with me when I first came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As I indicated, Mr. President, there is a time lapse between obtaining them and having them reproduced in this manner. I had asked that as soon as they were reproduced they should be handed to the Defence

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was five minutes ago, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, it was five minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it not have been -- may I just ask you a question. Don't you think that it would have been appropriate that even if you had to wait for 24 or 36 hours to have them reproduced, to immediately indicate to the Defence or to ask the assistance of the Chamber to speed up, because if you were aware of new photographs by yesterday morning, it should not be the case that the Defence only hears about the photographs as you have heard. I make a distinction between hearing about the existence of and having given access to copies of it. Do you agree with me that it is not appropriate to wait until five minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I agree and I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will see what consequences we have to draw out of this as far as the respect of the rights of the Defence are concerned. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These documents, these photographs that you are looking at, have a quick look through them, please. Are those four photographs that you brought and delivered to us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the reproductions of those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last two pages of the document that you have, please don't -- please have a look at the last two pages of the documents that you have. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Are those black and white reproductions of the same photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see writing on the three of those black and white reproductions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, below the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look -- well, before we get to that -- who made those writings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself. It is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the writing below the photograph with the number 02182301 and could you read it for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph number 1: "Zavnobih Square up until house number 18 where the shell landed approximately the east end side of the building."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And which building are you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the building where there was this make-shift classroom on the ground floor. Do you want me to explain any further? It is on the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I do apologise. Since my learned friend is asking about the pictures, is asking questions about the pictures, I would like the pictures to be placed on the ELMO because otherwise we don't know what the discussion is all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp did indicate the numbers, the numbers that are both in the bottom left, bottom corner of the photographs, and are also stamped on it. We have to be very careful to put them on the ELMO, I am afraid, especially in view of the photograph with the numbers ending in 300. But if it could be done -- but can't you follow it if the numbers are clearly indicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The problem is this: We've received a single copy and I believe that it would be a good idea for General Galic to follow this, and he is the only one who doesn't have the pictures in front of him. For the reasons you are familiar with, we only have one set. So if we could get a supplementary set of copies, we won't ask for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could temporarily provide a copy for General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So perhaps even without putting it on the ELMO, we then could proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. But I was going to ask just now the witness to put the photograph that we are referring to on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one would that be, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 301, yes. And then the -- I take it that you want the colour copy to be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, could you have a look at that document to your left and point to the building which is a school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the school is behind these blocks, so the classroom itself is surrounded by cement blocks on all sides. What can be seen on the picture is the eastern side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to the concrete structure in the foreground to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you point to the spot, if it is there, where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is here and I am indicating the explosion site. It can be seen on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to some markings in approximately the middle of the picture which is behind a dark area which appears to be the entrance of that structure he says is a make-shift school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That dark area on that photograph of that building in the foreground to the left, is that the entrance to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this dark part here?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a passage between -- between these slabs. The slabs are leaning against the roof of the building itself. It is a protruding part of the building. You would pass through here and there was a door here. It was the entrance to the building itself. Because this classroom was made -- it was an improvised one and it was a -- a business office was turned into this classroom. So this dark part in the photograph, it is just a passage to that entrance to the classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the black and white reproduction of your photographs and have a look at the writings under the photograph bearing the number 02182302. And could you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Photograph 2, site where the shell fell."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you have a look at the writing below the photograph numbered 02182303 and read it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Photograph 3, blood on the site beneath the slab."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document may be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we move on from here, can you tell us in a sentence what was the first photograph with the writings on it, photographs of an area where there are -- there was a certain amount of writings on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a photograph that wasn't shown on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, what is that photograph? And don't tell us what the writings are but tell us in a sentence what that photograph is about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That photograph shows part of the official registry in which the case was recorded. It says what happened, where it happened. It is in this registry that we have to make entries about what happened exactly, and we have to keep this in our premises. We have to note the exact date where it happened, when, when the case was concluded, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. You, that day, the 9th of November, 1993, you investigated any other scene of shelling in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you take photographs of that site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before I sit, may I just indicate to the Court that we have copies of those photographs available. We will not proceed to produce them, but they have been made available to the Defence and I understand the Defence have already used them. So at this stage, that concludes my cross-examination. May it please you, Mr. President, that concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp, I was just trying to understand your last words. I will just re-read them. You say the Defence already used them. That is what I did not fully understand, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the Defence used them to -- in the cross-examination of a previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These same photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not these. There is another set in respect to the other investigation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just a bit confused about what photographs you were referring to. Thank you then, Mr. Stamp. I am not going to ask whether the Defence is ready for cross-examining the witness, but I will ask whether they are ready to start the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are ready to start the cross-examination. Yes, we are ready to start the cross-examination, Mr. President. First of all, before starting the cross-examination, I see that the document that we have been provided with under 0282300, appears to -- appears to be a document that as the document -- as the Defence says has been manipulated in that the last vertical rectangle again appears to contain numbers which have been effaced. I have no other comments to make, but I am certain that there is an original somewhere and that perhaps one day it should be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are either now or in the later stage, of course, entitled to cross-examine the witness also on these kind of details.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Willingly, and I would like to add that these are not details in the view of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good day. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will go back to some of the things you spoke about just a minute ago. You told us that you had lived in what is called Alipasino Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you lived there for the entire period that we are interested in, 1993, 1994 -- 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I lived there during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that on the 15th of November 1995 you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you remember it in general? Can you remember the broad outline of this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I could remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, isn't it true that in the statement you said that you had taken photographs and that they had been made available to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had taken photographs and that they would all be made available to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we are talking about the 15th of November, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I suggest that we should perhaps present the document of which we have a copy, but which apparently the document -- the witness signed as a statement. But before doing that, I think I should mask something that we have written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also sign your witness -- your statement in the English version, did you also sign the English version of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. If you show it to me, I will tell you whether the signature is mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I remind you to switch off Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your microphone whenever the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, of course, thank you. I apologise. Mr. Usher, I need your assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to show you your statement. Could you just tell me whether you can see your initials there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am going to ask the usher to bring the document back to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please return the document to Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will return to the English document. That will make it possible for us to be more direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you had been a policeman and you said that, before that, you were a student. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that I stated that I was a student?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The Prosecution asked you a question yesterday and they asked you what you had been before becoming a policeman, and you said that you were a student and that you also had a private business. Is that correct? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is: What did you study?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What degree did you obtain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't finish my studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us about a private business. What was the nature of that business? Could you please tell us that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a commerce and services.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you be more precise, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would repair office equipment and we would sell such equipment, so cash registers, equipment that is needed for offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, were you involved in business during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in that kind of business during the war because I changed my place of residence, and everything that I had before the war remained at some other location, through no fault of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, a minute ago you spoke about or, rather, yesterday you spoke about investigations that you had carried out with regard to snipers and to sniper shells. Do you remember talking about this?
