utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember carrying out investigations into sniper shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You talked -- you told us about the necessity of having two traces to determine the direction. Do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that I spoke about this, about the fact that when you investigate sniping activity, I said it was necessary to have two traces in order to determine exactly where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Witness. Do you know the name of Mr. Kucanin? Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will return to that a little later. I am going back to the subject of projectiles. Within your service, were there any technical margins of error that were used when you would determine the direction from which a shot came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have such a device in order to determine areas when shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you say "I," should we take that to mean the police as a whole, those who cooperated with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Do you know whether your colleagues had such rules, rules which would include margins of error or such technical means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I am going to talk about Mr. Kucanin. You said that you knew him. Is this someone you would see? And I am talking in the past.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean whether I remember him?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Exactly, and whether you saw him in the past.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in an official capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you when you saw Mr. Kucanin for the last time or when you spoke to him for the last time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date, but I think that it was about a month ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was that after he had returned from The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Yes, it was. It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, could you please tell us what you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin had told me that he had been here and that he had made a statement. He wanted to meet with me and he wanted to sit down and have a chat. We had this meeting after quite a long period of time because I think that I hadn't seen him for a few years. I can't tell you exactly how long it had been since I last saw him. Kucanin did what he did and he doesn't have the same job any more. I continued to do my job, and believe me, the meeting was very brief. We didn't sit down anywhere but we only spent a little time together in the street. I know where we met. I know the exact place where we met, if you are interested in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That might interest everyone present here, but before talking about that, could you confirm whether he called you in your office? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't call him to at the office. We met quite my chance. I had other work at the time, other duties, and I met him at that place where we met. And he then told me his story. I didn't know that he had been here. That's when he told me he had been here. But he didn't go into the details. He didn't tell me any details about that when we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you spoke about what Mr. Kucanin might have said before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What did Mr. Kucanin tell you about the proceedings here in general and about his testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he had been here in the courtroom and he said he had given a statement. There wasn't enough time for him to tell me anything about that, but he did mention that we should meet. However, I didn't call him and I didn't have time to meet him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are quite categorical on this issue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I am just telling you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. With regard to this matter, do you know what the Zrak factory is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where it is and know more or less what was produced in that factory. But I was never there; I never entered that factory. I've passed by it and I know where it is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us where it is located and what it produced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the area. I think that it also belongs to the Novi Grad municipality area because I carried out a few on-site investigations over there, too. It is a factory which existed before the war broke out. I think that before the war, it produced -- and what I am saying now is what I heard. I think they produced optical devices for measurements of some kind. Whether it operated during the war, I don't know; I was never there, neither before the war, nor during the war, nor after the war. I've passed by it, yes, because there is a road that passes by the factory itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, we are going to show you a plan of Sarajevo, which we could put on the ELMO. And could you please -- could you please show us the location in question on this plan, perhaps with the assistance of the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. Do you recognise what you can see on the screen, that is to say part of the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. But I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why can't you see it well? Could we perhaps enlarge the image? Can you see now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you pinpoint the location we were talking about just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location, yes, I can. But the building, not exactly, but I could point to the location more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would be grateful if you could indicate this on the ELMO that you have on your right, on the map that is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area here, the exact place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the usher is going to show you -- is going to give you a colour -- a pen of a concern colour in a minute. And could you please encircle this area with the pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We are going to continue with this map. Witness, do you know school called Blagoje Parovic, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of it, yes. I think it is in the area of Novi Sarajevo, but I don't know where it is exactly. I think it is a primary school, but believe me, I don't know which street it is in or which area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you point to on the map that you have on your right, could you point to the zone in which this school was, as far as you can remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the area of the municipality of Ilidza and Novi Grad on the map and I think that the school was in the area of Novi Sarajevo but I don't know where exactly. There was also a street called Blagoje Parovic, but believe me, I don't know about that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Thank you for that answer. But you said you had heard of this school. Where, when and how did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was born in Sarajevo so I had heard of that school. Then I had heard of other schools which I never visited. And well, having heard of it, I don't necessarily have to know exactly where it is. What I mean to say well, Blagoje Parovic, but does the name of this school mean that it's in the Blagoje Parovic Street or that the school is called like that? It is a familiar name. I believe it was a primary school. But I have nothing of significance to be able to tell you in relation to that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know of a school which was called Pavle Goranin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am not certain but I think it is in the Otoka settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you show it on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the Otoka settlement can be seen on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Perhaps we will show you the second part of the map in a minute. Witness, are you familiar with a school called Petar Dakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. This brings me back to the first two names I have mentioned Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. earlier on. Do you know whether in one or the other, or in both of these establishments, there was a team of snipers from the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with it and I have not carried out any on-site investigations in those schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know in your capacity as police officer that the BH army also had a so-called sniper unit? When I say "Oza," that means just as well as the other units, some other units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a police officer, I am not familiar with the structure of the army or what they had. But perhaps as an armed force they might have had companies organised like that, but I am unable to tell you anything about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether the so-called BH army also had specialised units for mortar, that is to say specialised mortar battalions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I was a police officer and it is an altogether different job. My job was completely different so I really can't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. For what reason were you not mobilised to join the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where the Cenex building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cenex had several buildings. I don't know which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The one which is closest to the school I have mentioned earlier, the first school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cenex had a building -- well, I don't know if it was the entire building. It was a building on pillars and it was in the area of Novo Sarajevo municipality, near the bakery, supposedly. Is that the building you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map where this Cenex building near Stup is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't show you this Cenex because it is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, then, thank you, Witness. Witness, are you familiar with the name of Mr. Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who was he, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, he was the commander of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever been under orders of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I have never met this man in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when exactly did you join the police force and when did you start work as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the police force in 1993, and as to the exact date when I got the letter telling me I could start work. I can't remember. I believe it was in the second half of 1993 when I was informed of my having been accepted in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you remind us of the date when the hostilities first started in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. You've mentioned that you joined the police force in the second half of 1993. What were you doing between April 1992 and the second half of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent 1992 staying with my cousins, with my family, as a refugee from Dobrinja IV, up until the point where I had to register with someone. And it was in January of 1993 I joined the police force. That was when I could start the seminar for this job. And upon completion of that seminar, I got the official letter and as of that date, I am registered as an active policeman. In other words, I couldn't have been considered as an active police officer before finishing the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So if my understanding is correct, you went on a six-month course starting in January 1993 and then you joined the police force for all intents and purposes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I went on a six-month course. I can't tell you exactly whether it started in January or not. There was some preparation going on. I can't remember the exact date when we first started but it lasted for barely six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. What did you do between April 1992 and January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, I was trying to survive, and I did say I was staying with relatives, I was a refugee.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there not a general mobilisation order very soon after the start of the hostilities in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the exact date was. I know I've tried everything because I suffered a great deal at that time when I had to leave my original residence from before the war, not just myself, but my entire family, were trying to simply survive and make ends meet. As to this mobilisation as to whether it was a forced one, I can't talk much about that. I can tell you what I myself did. In the time I joined the police force, it was extremely difficult to even be able to qualify for the job, which I still hold.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I do understand, Witness, but is it not correct that there was proclamation according to which all men of a certain age had to report to the closest barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with it and I never reported that -- well, actually, when I first got there, I had to register at the settlement where I was living, the municipal offices. As to where those lists were taken, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, have you collaborated in any way with what is normally called the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the speaker please speak a bit closer to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I had to. I had to collaborate with the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you incorporated within a unit, not of the Civil Defence as it appears in the transcript, but the Territorial Defence, TEO? That's the Serb acronym, TEO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not belong to any of their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. I would now like to pursue another line of reasoning. In your capacity as a police officer, you said you travelled both within this area that is of interest to us and in other parts of Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you have an official car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I mean, could your service make available cars in case you needed them on the job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: In very rare cases, I did carry out on-the-spot investigations and I used any vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why do you say, "on extremely rare occasions"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: My job was in the centre of town. Since the entire area of the city had been shelled, that was the decision made within my department to have us work close to where we lived. And since at the time I lived in the area of Alipasino Polje, the best thing was for me and a couple of my colleagues was to work in that area. So for a certain period of time, I spent also in Novi Grad, at the Novi Grad police station, but my permanent job and my original department was in the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Just very briefly, where did you get fuel and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never got it anywhere. When investigations were carried out, I used the official car from the police station of Novi Grad, whereas my department belonged to the security service. If I needed a car, I would have to get in touch with Novi Grad people and ask them to take me there or for me to be given a vehicle. But I never had to get petrol. If there was a vehicle available, I would use it. If there were none, I couldn't use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, looking at the clock, if you would find a suitable moment somewhere in the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have a break for 20 minutes. I would like to have a break for 20 minutes starting somewhere in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can break now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 5.59 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like us to continue with some further questions. I would like to come back to the two squares that you have mentioned earlier, that is to say the one which was called Rade Koncara Square and the other one which I believe was called Zavnobih. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether in one of those situations the army had the means to manufacture arms, I mean any workshops where those arms could have been manufactured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether in one or the other of those two squares there were any canteens that could have been used by the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of any premises used by the army in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether in one or the other of those two squares the army had any administrative offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, soldiers travelled throughout the city, and exactly as to where their buildings and premises were, I can't tell you. There were some premises possibly someplace, but I can't tell you where exactly because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you lived in Alipasino Polje. Did you at the time used to see soldiers in the area of Alipasino Polje frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were they armed and in uniform or armed without uniform, or did they appear in any other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, they were uniformed. Even I had that uniform because there were no other clothes available. And we called it work clothes, not uniforms. There were quite a few people wearing those clothes who did other jobs, and I can't tell you exactly whether they were armed or not. There were quite a few people who moved about carrying guns. And as to any heavy weaponry, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say people walking around town carrying arms, you mean uniformed people or civilians without uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, uniformed people carried arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But since you said "for the most part," I assume that there were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. also civilians who were armed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The clothes, the work clothes, the uniforms, everything was worn. As to everybody wearing uniforms being a soldier, I don't know, I can't remember. I can't remember about people wearing civilians clothes. At the very beginning, there were no uniforms at all and people would wear their own clothes and they would carry arms as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this reply. Witness, I'd like to submit to you -- but in order to speed things up and simplify matters, I have photocopies. So I would like to submit to you two documents which have already been mentioned on another occasion, D55 and D81, and we have got a couple of copies for everybody concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I may, Mr. President, we can have them circulated with the assistance of the usher, who I can see is rushing towards me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D81, I have as a diagram of Markale market. Is that the one you wish?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There must be an error there. Could you give me these papers back? They were prenumbered. We are going to check it out on the list. D81, according to our reference - but perhaps it is a mistake - should be an order coming from 102nd Motorised Brigade from January 1993 -- sorry, the 4th of June, 1993. If that is not on the list, we are going to submit it under a new number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is available to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not carefully listened. Do you remember the date on which --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague is looking for it. We have found the number, and if it had not been produced before, we are going to do it now. The date when it was first produced should be the 1st of March, I believe -- or the 3rd of March, for D55, at any rate. But now I am looking through the list of documents. I haven't checked it out myself. Yes, indeed, there is a mistake there. I am going to try to check what the correct number is. As a matter of fact, I would like to start with number 55, and the rest of it is going to be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, it is not D81, but apparently D54. The second document, I mean. And we will see it a bit more clearly later. Could you take a look at D55, please? Witness, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: D55, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it in a language that you can understand? Is it the English translation you have in front of you or is it the original?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the English document in front of me and I have got a copy enclosed to this translation, something in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... continuing. Could we just have a look at the original for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a problem, Mr. President? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree that this document mentions the command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't agree with that because all I can see is that in English it says, "the command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade." I can see that on the paper in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you take the text in Serbian? Take the Serbian text. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this here. It says: "The command of the 102nd Motorised Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you please have a look at the fourth line which follows item one, so the fourth line after the "communications centre," after what is written down as "communications centre."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you found the sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third or the fourth line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The fourth line underlined.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "At the command post of the 1st Infantry Brigade in

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Polje, Alipasino Polje connected to the post office in Sarajevo all the time and the main staff of the B --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the abbreviations, Witness, the ones at the end. Just the abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The command post of the 1st Motorised Brigade, the main staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree that in the area of Alipasino Polje there was a command post, what one usually calls a command and control post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with that. All I could do was read this here. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you know where you can find the command post of the 102nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could we please present the document with the number D97. Could the usher please assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have it both in the Serbian version and in the English version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in a language which I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, could you tell us what you can see under item seven in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "the Stela base, [Zavno BH Square 17]."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what was the distance between this number 17, how far was this number 17 from the incidents which you mentioned a while ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the case that I -- well, this is an uneven number, an odd number. I don't think that the numbers have changed to this day. I don't know how far it was from number 17. It should be on the other side of the square. I know that square. I have passed through it quite often and I still do. But I don't know exactly where the entrance at number 17 would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Doesn't Stela refer to a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. In your capacity of a policeman who visited the area, were you able to pinpoint this restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an observer. I was just carrying out an investigation when I got there. But Stela, I think that there was a cafe there, it was a cafe called Stela before the war, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how far is it from the cafe that you know and the site of impact approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 50 and 100 metres. I couldn't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for this answer. Witness, you told us that you yourself had found the stabiliser; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I am talking about one of the cases that you investigated and you said that you found the stabiliser at the site; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't personally find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does this concern the incident for which you said you were one of the first to arrive at the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually, as I was closest to the site, I was in the Novi Grad Public Security Station, I tried to get there first before the other members of the team because the other members of the team came by car from the town. I think that if I had found that part of the shell at the site, it would have been photographed. But it is possible that it was given to a member of the investigations team, and on that basis I mentioned that an explosion had been -- had occurred and I mentioned what the calibre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you yourself see this stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who was it given to as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That stabiliser, I took that stabiliser and it was put away in the department in which I worked and this is what I stated in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of collecting what one calls mortar balls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, in the case which I took over that stabiliser, well, investigations were carried out in such conditions that it was quite possible for there to be renewed shelling so that the shrapnel, obviously, it wasn't -- they weren't at the site of the explosion itself. They would be dispersed. In most cases it was necessary to investigate the site itself. Finding the shrapnel was an especially dangerous task because it was possible for the shelling to recommence and that would have put in danger the lives of the investigators and the members of the investigating team.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We are going to provide you with document number 98 with regard to this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D98, English translation, D98.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is this one of the incidents that we have spoken about when you were examined by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you remind us which incident is in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an incident that took place on the 22nd of January, 1994. The Cetinska and Klara Zetkin streets were shelled, that is to say Cetinska and Klara Zetkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I think I heard you say just a minute ago that given the conditions that prevailed, you had to work on your own at the site. Is that quite correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true that I worked alone at the site. I was only able to visually inspect what was at the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you alone when carrying out this inspection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't know whether there were other specialists with you, ballistic experts or specialists of another kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later on. But before then, I got there before them with colleagues from the Public Security station in Novi Grad who were also present at the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us how much later after you the colleagues arrived there, the colleagues who are mentioned in the report that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly when the team arrived and assembled.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you confirm that these persons were present at the site Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons who have been listed here, yes, they were at the site with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the special expert was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Borislav Stankov.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, just a minute ago with regard to the questions concerning ballistics, you said that you could, generally speaking, identify the direction from which shots came, given your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on the basis of the traces left by the explosion of certain projectiles. It is only on this basis that it is possible to determine the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, didn't you say that - I think in your statement of the 15th of November, 1995 - that with regard to the incident that we are talking about, the direction of the shell in ballistic terms came over the positions, the shell came over the positions held by the Serbian army but also over the positions held by the so-called BH army. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think that question could only be fairly put if my friend directs the witness to which of the shelling incidents that he is speaking about. The witness has testified to investigating four impact sites and perhaps three shelling incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was I right in understanding, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you were talking about the incident of the 22nd of January, 1994? Yes. That became clear to me from the line of questioning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will go back to this question. Witness, is it true that you said the direction from which the shell came or what you thought was the direction from which the shell came, it could have, in technical terms, come from both of the camps because the trajectory included two possible sources, two possible origins: both the Serbian party, the so-called Serb part, and the so-called BH part? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on the basis of the traces found, one would determine the direction and in the settlement I already mentioned was already in that direction. I didn't mention the place from which the shell was fired though.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, didn't you say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, are you going to read because that very often avoids a lot of confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, maybe a little later, but I am going to address this matter without reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... pause after the question so that the Prosecution is able to follow what part of the statement you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly. Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, didn't you say that this was a technique used by the Serbs: They would position themselves near the positions of the Muslim forces in order to create confusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am going to read out something. I want to check that there are no problems with regard to the names in the statement and I would like to be authorised to do so in order to avoid any confusion. Could you allow me 30 seconds, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And since it appears that my friend wishes to confront the witness with something in his statement, I would ask that the particular incident where any comment might be made about in that statement is given to the witness. If the witness is to be confronted with a statement or a part of a statement, then that particular incident should be told to the witness so that the witness may be able to put it in context. I am quite sure that my friend won't put anything to the witness out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you are more or less asking me to give instructions to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. What I did, as a matter of fact, is that I asked Mr. Piletta-Zanin to at least pause and perhaps ask the witness to wait for a second so that you can check whether there finally the question is such that you would have to object against it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am going to quote what the witness said. I would just like to verify this, if we put the document on the screen, there aren't any names that could be problematic. This might take a little while. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going to read what you said, Witness, on the 15th of November, 1995 and I am going to read it because you spoke of a general tactic and this concerns both the incident of the 9th of November, 1993 of which you have spoken here in Alipasino Polje and it also concerns other incidents, including the one that occurred in January. I am going to read this out in English. [In English] "The BSA to fire shells from close to our positions to confuse the investigators." [Interpretation] Witness, do you remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what it says in my statement, then I did, but I can't remember the exact date -- details. After all, that was seven years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In other words, Witness, if according to your statement you said that such and such shell came from a position which was close to so-called Muslim positions or a so-called Muslim position, would you agree that theoretically, it was also possible -- it would also be possible for this shell to have come from a Muslim position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to agree with anything in particular. All I did was my job. Where the shell came from, well, there are ballistic experts to determine that. They can determine this on the basis of other elements. They can determine where the shell was fired from. My job was to investigate the site. If I stated something like that, something like what you have just read out, that was an opinion of mine that I expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to -- I am going to provide you with this page and I would like you to identify your signature, please, because I think that you are putting to question what you stated at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is in English but I can see my initials here and I said that I wasn't contesting this. If that's what it states, then, yes, the statement is mine. It's been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. In that case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please return the statement to Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I don't think you have answered my question. It is therefore theoretically possible that such a shell came from a line which was held by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, you mentioned the diameter -- I apologise -- calibre, 120 millimetre calibre. Do you stand by this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you stand by what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that I mentioned a 120 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether other experts from your group found a 120 millimetre calibre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I found it out, but on the basis of the report from the ballistics expert that there were other calibres in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please repeat your question because there might be some confusing -- your question was: "Do you know whether other experts from your group found a -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not 120 millimetre. It's an 82 millimetre calibre. We have a problem with the figures today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what I have. This could create confusion. So the question is whether his colleague found an 82 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have already answered the question but is it correct that other experts found other calibres, calibres which were not 120 millimetre calibres and they stated that the calibres in question were 82 millimetre calibres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read in the report from the ballistics experts that the calibres in question were 82 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Witness. Witness, I would like to turn back to the two squares that we mentioned a minute ago, the Rade Koncara Square and Zavnobiha. There was a question I haven't asked you. As far as you know, were there any premises used by the police in those squares? And as a policeman, as citizen, you might be able to provide us with an answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I think that in the Rade Koncara Square, there was a department of some kind. Whether it was a police station, I am not sure because I never went there. It was department of the uniformed police but I don't belong to that department so I can't claim this with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what do you call a department, a section? Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there was some sort of station of the uniformed police there for that area. And perhaps they went on shifts there because everything was done in order to prevent people from moving in order to make sure that people didn't have to move too much because of the shelling. But how many people were, and up until when, I am not really in a position to say. Nor can I say who issued an order or how many people were there. But this is just my opinion. I really don't know whether there was such a place. I know that a department -- there was no department of the criminal police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, thank you for this answer. You said that it was necessary for the people to move as little as possible. Do I understand you correctly if I say that in a certain sense there was a dissolution of the various police stations and the various command posts in the town, that these places broke up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand when you say "command post." There were several police stations, public security stations. They existed before the conflict and they still exist now. But there are police administrations now. There's the public security station in Novi Grad and there's one in Nova Sarajevo, in Centar, in Stari Grad -- there are public security stations in all these places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- if I may interrupt you. I am trying to think at what we are going to do today and in the few coming days. I know that if the cross-examination of the witness would take until 7.00, that you would have used less time than the examination-in-chief. On the other hand, the examination-in-chief Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. included the examination of the witness on the new photographs, so I take it that if you want to reserve some time for that as well, well, there would be 10 to 15 minutes left. I also know that it has been scheduled to, when possible, to examine an expert for two days you indicated approximately. So if we would start with that tomorrow and two days that would take us until the -- up until Friday in the afternoon. So I am just wondering what -- how much time you would still need. And of course, as I said, if you want to study with the photographs, we will hear from you later on whether there are any additional questions to be put in that respect or whether the witness shall be recalled, whatever problem we'll face then. We can't predict that. But could you give us an indication on whether on the part of the cross-examination not dealing with the photographs, you think you could do it until 7.00 or... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, we are going to finish by 7.00 and even before perhaps. There is just one question with regard to the new photographs and therefore it is -- it will be necessary to call this witness later. We only have one series of questions concerning the new photograph

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed for this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just very rapidly, sir, as not to waste anyone's time. My question was the following: Do you know whether during the war there was a policy of distributing various police stations, scattering them about the city in order to avoid having people to move about too much?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with any army or military posts that you refer to in your question. I know that there was a Public Security station in Novi Grad and Novi Sarajevo and all the other Public Security stations and our police stations which are situated where they used to be in the past. So this is the usual distribution of police stations, the structure that was in existence prior to these facilities. I work in that sector myself so each police station and public security station has its own department for the criminal police and those are the people that I worked with. But I don't know anything about the military structure or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, with reference to each and every one of these incidents that we've discussed, do you know whether your services, general speaking, would have called the UNPROFOR services in order to work together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I don't have the competence to answer that question because I am a member of the investigation team. It was up to others to make up the team. And other people used to make the relevant calls. The head of the team would be the investigating magistrate, and in case the magistrate would not visit the site in question, it would be led by the inspector of the public security services in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether on a regular basis there would be reports filed and submitted to the investigating magistrate indicating the results of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the team leader, whether it was a magistrate or an inspector, would be obliged to draw up a report. It would be the team leader's task, and such a report would be drawn up after the on-site investigation. As to what would happen later once my own report would come in, the ballistic expert report came in and all that, I suppose all that together would make up the file. I am not really familiar with what the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was that the case for this particular incident in 1993 as far as you can tell? There were two incidents, for both of them, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who drew up the report. I can tell you what I did. Once again, I believe that the investigating magistrate did not draw up the report. It was the inspector, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So the so-called regular standard procedure of resorting to a magistrate was not followed in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just in this case. The regular standard procedure would be for the team to be made of the investigating magistrate, the prosecutor, the inspector, the forensic expert, and all the various experts, depending on the needs. And the actual procedure in case the investigating magistrate would not visit the scene, the report would then be drawn up by the inspector of the public security services or else somebody from the police station. I mean, there are relevant legal provisions laying down the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, then, thank you, Witness. Now to come back to these incidents that we are discussing at the moment, both in November and in January. Do you know whether any measures were implemented in order to get in touch with the opposite party and organise a commission of the inquiry of international nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On the other hand, can you confirm what you have just said, that is to say, that since energy problems were serious in Sarajevo, it was not always possible for you to be up to date when it came to the news, to listen to the media and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I have one last series of questions with reference to the document that we are just received, but only about the so-called mechanical side of things, what we normally call manipulation. Let me just specify once again that we can't accept this document, but in spite of that, we have to ask these questions because it is an even more important principle that it is at stake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we submit 0282300 to the witness. Unfortunately, I have to hang on to my copy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Are you referring to Exhibit P3681?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is exactly that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you take a look at this document. On the left-hand side, can you see a pillar which is larger than the others, or rather a column where there is a handwritten text?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I can read everything. I don't know what precisely you are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I am interested in the last square at the bottom of the page, starting with the word "Dona" and followed by the number 9. Do you see that square, that box?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. I would like you to read for the sake of the transcript the words which precede that particular box, that is to say, what is included in the previous rectangular shape. Can you read it because we do not have a perfect translation of that text -- or, rather, we don't have it at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Trg Zavnobiha 18."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, that is not what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you are asking to read the previous rectangular shape, you can either go upwards or to the left. I don't know which one you wanted the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right. I meant the box which is -- which precedes this one to the left and it starts with the words starting with a "B." To the left of what I have just read.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left of what I read earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, to the left with regard to the word "Dona."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I did read. To the left with reference to Dona is the square Zavnobiha house number 18 below.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And then to the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that all these big rectangulars start with the word "Dona." That might create some confusion. You are asking the witness to read at the bottom line, and we start, Mr. Q, at the left. The first box is a 9, yes? You agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second, the third, the fourth and then the fifth box, would you please read that. Is that what you intended him to read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the fifth one, that would be square 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, down below. Go all the way down to the bottom of this document, Witness, and you will see a word starting with a letter "B." Can you find it? It ends by "Kazani."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not one of my cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I do know that it is not one of your cases, but in spite of that, I would like to kindly read this Bogusevac Jama Kazani. I did not hear the translation. I would like it to be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you read it slowly, the same word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bogusevac Jama Kazani. It appears to be a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, would you like to read down to the right of what you are just read. It starts again with "Dona," the day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the day of the 9th of November, 1993, at Bogusevac Jama Kazani, 24 NN corpses were extracted, plus two heads."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "NN," does it not stand for unidentified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: NN, yes, unidentified, unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you tell us what Kazani stands for? Sometimes it is associated with the caves of Kazani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not know. I cannot answer that question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. If I tell you that Kazani was the mass grave where Serbs were buried, had been discovered, does it remind you of anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about it. I was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You do know this area, where is it? You know these documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the official register where we register our cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to concentrate on the box down below that you have just read. Don't you see under this number 24, other numbers or other indications, as it were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I read earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Under "24."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Don't you see, Witness, below the number 24 underneath there is a trace of something having been erased or deleted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see some traces but I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. And one last question, Mr. President. And we will necessarily have to come back to this. Witness, do you know where the original of this page might be found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the original -- well, the original would be in the register at my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does it still exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with the register when I was entering my own cases, the reports pertaining to my own cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is this your own handwritten document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The one up there, the case that you dealt with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But to a certain extent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the part at the right. It is my handwriting in the penultimate section, in the upper part of the paper, and the rest of it, I dictated it to the colleagues that were doing up the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you yourself copied or photocopied this page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I copied when I was preparing --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine, since I know nothing about your preparations, can you nevertheless tell me when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perhaps a month ago. I can't tell exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So a month ago these documents still existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will take note of that, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions. I do apologise to everyone for this delay, and we'll no doubt have to recall this witness for the reasons you are familiar with, and we have no questions for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just confer for one single second with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Q, you might have noticed that the document you were just questioned about has both the interest of the Prosecution and, perhaps for other reasons, but also the interest of the Defence. It is tendered into evidence, copies of this document by the Prosecution, so we have to decide on that. But in case we would decide that this document will be admitted in evidence, we just have a photocopy here. And since we understand that the original is under your control, this Chamber gives you an order to keep it under your control and to have it available, the original, for inspection by the Tribunal. You did understand what I just said, that you copied it, the original; you should keep it. So we order you not to lose it, not to destroy it, not to give it away as a birthday present, whatever. It should stay where it is and you should keep it under your control. And this is an order of the Chamber of the Tribunal, one that you are bound to fulfill. Do you have any questions in respect of that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. I don't have the original. It is a register of all the official activities situated in Sarajevo. It is not within my competence to take it out without the approval from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not asking you to take out anything. I think you said that it was in your offices. You don't have to take it out. But we order you to do everything in order to be sure that no one else takes it out as well, so neither yourself or anyone else, and if necessary, we would expand this order to your superiors as well. What we want to avoid is that we are later on in a position where questions are still there in respect of this document and whether the original was available. Until very recently, copies could be made and could be produced in this court that suddenly the original wasn't there any more. That is what the order was about. You are bound by this order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to state that it is not within my competence to keep or preserve this document in any way. If it is within your power to get in touch with my superiors directly to make sure that that document is preserved, fine, but it is not up to me. I believe that this register referring to that particular period of time has been stored in the archives and it is only my superiors who can issue any orders in relation to that register. I am not in a position to get my hands on it without their permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Q, what this Chamber knows is that you gave testimony that you copied it, so that you have some kind of control. And whatever one of your superiors says that they want to take it away or to do anything else with it, that you should tell them that you are bound by an order of this Court to do whatever you whatever you can do to prevent them. If some of your superiors would think that -- well, if it would disappear, that that would be a very serious matter and that would be keeping away from this Chamber potential original evidence, or even worse, destroying potential evidence which is -- which would result in contempt of this Court. Yes. I apologise for the interpreters that we took seven minutes extra without asking your permission. I should have done so. But you also may have noticed it was a bit of an exceptional situation. May I just ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, at this very moment -- no, perhaps, first ask the witness to be guided out of the court and with the -- at this moment, you are not yet excused because there might be some additional questions from either the Prosecution or the Defence or the Judges. So that means that you should return to this courtroom by tomorrow a quarter past 2.00. And how much it would then will take, we will see whether you have to come back at perhaps a later moment, we will also see. But would you please come back tomorrow by a quarter past 2.00. There is another order: You should not get in touch with your superiors or your colleagues in order to inform them about the order you were given. That might create additional problems. Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I make it quite briefly, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you said you would like to come back to this document at a later moment. I do think you would like to do it right tomorrow after you further inspected the document, or do you say, well, I'll see whether it will be necessary to recall the witness at a later moment or whether I can conclude the cross-examination by tomorrow on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let's adopt a pragmatic approach because at any rate this witness will have to come back. If let's say we have him come back in a couple of days or in a couple of weeks, perhaps in that case he could bring along the original and that would perhaps be the best possible way to clarify certain matters. I believe that we are ready - I can't confirm - I mean, we can continue the cross-examination tomorrow, but this other option would be useful as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine that you -- I think we have to consider your observation, but could we at least hear from you tomorrow by 2.15 on whether you have any additional questions at this moment in relation to this document, at least alone whether there are other questions to be put either to this witness or other witnesses in respect of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have further questions, that is certain. We will see how much time is necessary and we will let you know tomorrow morning, early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, I take it that you will need some time for re-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I -- no, I don't think there would be much depending on what is asked. So far, there is hardly anything. We note the cross-examination of the document. We can't see it being relevant to the issues in this case. There might be issues for other cases. However, that is a matter for a judgment. I could say that we don't have much in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. So what --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp. We are asking a lot from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is one clarification, if I may ask about the order which you made. If I understood it, it was indicated by the witness that he did not have control of these documents. This is from a register which is kept in an archive and that his superiors would have to make a decision as to what happens. And subsequently, I believe he was told that he could not inform his superiors of the order which the Court made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He should not get in touch with his superiors. It might be quite clear to you what is the concern of this Court. What we try to achieve is to prevent that would happen what would be of major concern to us, that it means preservation of evidence. As a matter of fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The order has been given by the Chamber and we will discuss, we'll have some deliberations on what the consequences should be because there have been suggested different solutions that the witness would bring. Perhaps he might not have the power. But perhaps there are other ways of inspecting, or at least to see whether originals can be inspected. And as you may have noticed, the concern of the Court is that the original remains available in whatever form, whatever way, either for the parties to inspect first or to be produced to the Court. That is the major concern of this Chamber. Whether we need any additional orders to give, you will hear that by tomorrow. I also wanted to prevent the witness to give a lot of phone calls this evening and that unfortunately evidence might be lost. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Then I take it that tomorrow -- may I take it that approximately half an hour with re-examination and, if necessary, questions of the Judges -- that we could spend half an hour on Witness Q and then proceed with the expert, Mr. Donia. We will adjourn and I thank both the technicians and the interpreters for their patience. We will adjourn until 2.15 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.15, p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th, day of April, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
